name: Control Console
description: A small Dieter-Rams CONSOLE — a brushed grey-metal CSG cabinet with a warm Braun control plate recessed flush in its slanted face, on a base plinth. Built like the pattern machines' display console with CSG booleans (a block minus a reclined wedge for the angled screen face, minus a shallow pocket for the bezel) so the plate sits INSIDE the metal, framed, not floating. The plate gives the controls a home; the console gives the whole instrument one. By default it shows a reference instrument (title + SCALE k slider + SNAP button + green-LED readout); a teaching machine can house its own controls inside it via the same add_slider / add_button / add_readout API.
theoreticalGrounding: A layout is not a set of positions, it is a set of relationships. The box model nests: a console contains a plate, which contains a row of cells, which contain controls. Once the relationships are modelled, the positions compute themselves and the housing reads as one designed object.

control_console.name: Control Console
control_console.description: Brushed grey-metal CSG cabinet (CSGCombiner3D: block - reclined wedge - shallow pocket) housing the canonical Braun ControlPanel recessed in its slanted face, on a dark base plinth. Forwards add_slider / add_button / add_dial / add_joystick / add_readout / set_title to the inner plate and provides the reading tilt itself. Default demo content: title + SCALE k slider + SNAP button + a green-LED 2D-in-3D readout. DNA: title, tilt_deg, body_color.
control_console.qfep_connection: The instrument that holds the instrument — a relational frame that gives the controls a body, a face, a base. The box model one level up.

dna.default: mounting=kiosk, demo_apparatus=none - the shipped build node for node: the CSG base box rising to the head's lower-front edge, the dark plinth lip, the cabinet door with its pull handle, the four vent slats, and no apparatus in front. Both new branches are additive `if mounting == "kiosk"` guards around code that is otherwise byte-identical, so the 4 map placements are unchanged AND so are the 14 workbench artifacts that compose this script directly (shannon_workbench, halting_workbench, stretch_bench, riemann_sum_workbench, ...), none of which sets mounting.
dna.was: a floor-standing metal cabinet, asserted before the question was asked. Twenty-one exports, every one of them a dimension, a colour or a nudge - four separate knobs (board_drop, board_out, board_slide, board_face_drop) for moving the same plate a centimetre - and not one of them asking whether an interface must also be a container. Every workbench that composes this console inherited a door and a vent grille whether or not the room wanted an appliance.
dna.note: mounting reuses soft_stage_dashboard's word and its three answers character for character; the two measure alike (wall removes the body, lectern puts the face on legs, kiosk gives it a standing body) and only the DEFAULT differs, because the dashboard shipped as a bare quad and this shipped as a cabinet. demo_apparatus was already an @export with a match block and had never been declared, so the sweep could not reach it. Its four non-none values now derive viz_floor from face_to_origin, because the -1.0 default is a DESKTOP assumption that sank every apparatus base a metre under a floor-standing console.
